results.title: Canva bucks tech employment slowdown with 'intentional' global hiring spree — Capital Brief
results.author: Bronwen Clune
highlights:
While much of the global software-as-a-service (SaaS) sector is pulling back on headcount, Australia’s design juggernaut Canva is pressing ahead with an aggressive global expansion, advertising more than 300 open roles and snapping up senior talent from rivals including Figma and Adobe.

Those 300-plus roles span product, artificial intelligence, enterprise and international teams, with a heavy emphasis on overseas growth across the US, Europe, Latin America and the Asia-Pacific.

...

Canva now employs more than 5,500 staff globally. Headcount grew 6% last year, even as the broader technology sector shed more than 245,000 jobs worldwide in 2025.

The current vacancies represent more than 5% of Canva’s existing workforce — a far higher proportion than larger competitors such as Adobe, which has about 625 open roles across a workforce of more than 30,000.

results.title: Canva's Sydney smoke signal
results.author: Amelia McGuire
highlights:
Australia's largest technology company Canva has started formally preferencing Sydney-based applicants for some departments after years of generous flexible work arrangements. 

In any other company this wouldn't mean much at all. Corporations everywhere have slowly been clawing back the flexible working arrangements they extended during COVID-19 to mixed success. 

But Canva is not like any other company. It calls staff "Canvanauts", its executives communicate with emojis and offer cash allowances to "vibe and thrive". And while many of the 5,500 employees have grown accustomed to the ability to work from anywhere, Canva has also been grappling with the global artificial intelligence reckoning and increased pressure on software companies everywhere to become more efficient.

results.title: Canva's free users started costing money, and 1,271 jobs... | Tech Twitter
results.author: Aakash Gupta
highlights:
# Canva's free users started costing money, and 1,271 jobs went

Aakash Gupta@aakashgupta · November 4, 2026 · 7 min read

Originally published by @aakashgupta on X.

Canva just cut 1,271 people, about 22% of the company, a few months after free users piled into its new AI tools, which cost Canva real money every single time someone typed a prompt.

Canva had about 5,800 employees before today. Melanie Perkins called this “the hardest moment in our thirteen-year history,” and she told staff growth had slowed for the first time in a decade.

...

Then in August, Blackbird and Airtree marked Canva down from $42 billion to $34.9 billion. That's $7.1 billion, about 17%, wiped off. The internal price employees can sell their shares at went from $38.9 billion to $31 billion, and now the IPO talk is about next year.

...

So the same AI wave pushed Canva's costs up and gave some of its users a free alternative, both at once.

What happened today

The memo doesn't blame AI for the cuts, and Canva didn't say AI took anybody's job. The 1,271 number also counts role changes and people being asked to relocate, so some of it isn't straight layoffs.

The memo mostly shrinks and flattens the org chart. Product, growth and platform get merged into one product organization. Perkins said years of growth left them with too many management layers and too many handoffs. More product roles are moving to Sydney, and starting January 2027 most hybrid staff are expected in the office two to three days a week.

I'll give Perkins credit on how she handled the exits, it's about as decent as these things get. People who are leaving get at least six months of pay, a year of healthcare where Canva already offers it, and a year of the employee assistance program for their families too. If you joined in the past year, the one-year vesting cliff is waived. There's a $10,000 grant to start a business or community project, with Canva taking zero equity, and people get to keep their MacBooks.

results.title: An important update on our team
highlights:
Today, I have some profoundly difficult news to share.

After months of thinking through how to set Canva up for the next chapter, we have made the incredibly hard decision to make significant changes to how we’re organised, where some of our teams are based, and the roles and skills we need for the future.

This means 1,271 people, or 22% of Canva, will be impacted. For some people, this will mean changes to their roles or being asked to relocate to centralised hubs. Sadly, it will also mean saying goodbye to teammates and friends who have helped build Canva into what it is today.

...

After exploring a wide range of alternatives, I've come to the difficult conclusion that small changes won’t be enough. To set ourselves up for the next decade, we need to refound Canva, getting back to our roots of small, empowered teams with the freedom to make decisions, take ownership and focus on what matters most for our community.

...

### What we’re changing

We're making three changes to bring more of what has made Canva special back into how we work.

#1. We're simplifying how we come together to build Canva

As we've grown, more of our work has become organised around team structures and narrow areas of ownership. Improving one part of our product often requires navigating between Product, Growth and Platform, with more handovers and coordination than necessary. This has made it harder to take ownership of bigger problems and to build a deeply unified product for our community. We’ve tried many ways to solve this over the years, but it’s become clear we need to revisit our underlying structure.

To do that, we’re bringing Product, Growth and Platform together into one Product Org and changing the way we work to provide clearer ownership, greater autonomy and flexibility to tackle our most important goals. We want to get back to spending more time building, and less time navigating how work gets done.

...

#3. We’re co-locating closely connected teams and increasing in-person collaboration

Working across countries has brought enormous benefits and talent, but it’s also made it harder to bring the right people together to solve complex problems. We’ll continue investing in our global team, particularly where being close to our community, customers and markets matters most.

At the same time, Sydney will become the primary home for more of our product teams, as well as roles in other Specialties where shared context and close collaboration are especially important. We know relocating is a big decision for those being asked to consider it, and we're committed to making the process as smooth as possible with comprehensive support.

...

We've put together some answers to common questions and everything you need to know. There's no need to read through everything right now, but we hope they'll be helpful whenever you're ready. Next week, we’ll come together for a Company All Hands on November 10th to talk through these changes, answer questions, and share more about the path ahead. We’ve asked Org Leads to wait until after this to bring their teams together, with Org All Hands taking place from November 11th.

results.title: Sobering markdown: Canva slashes valuation by $10b as AI reality bites - 𝕹𝖆𝖙𝖎𝖔𝖓 𝕺𝖚𝖙𝖑𝖔𝖔𝗸
results.author: nationoutlook
highlights:
The number Canva gave staff is a 409A valuation, an independent price US tax rules require before a private company can hand shares to employees. It is designed to sit below what investors would pay because staff shares cannot easily be sold.

Canva will use it to price this year’s share grants to its roughly 5500 employees, due within a fortnight. Many hold options once expected to make them millionaires when the company floats.
